name: Anthropic Python SDK Course
//: Comments here use JSON-safe "//" keys (not // line comments) so this file parses with any strict JSON reader, including python3 -c 'import json; json.load(...)'.
// image: Python 3.11 on Debian bookworm. The course needs 3.9+; 3.11 is a safe, fast, well-supported floor.
// postCreateCommand: Runs ONCE when the container is first built: install the SDK + python-dotenv, then create .env from .env.example only if .env does not already exist (never clobber a key the learner already pasted in).
postCreateCommand: python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip && python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt && { [ -f .env ] || cp .env.example .env; } && echo 'postCreate: dependencies installed, .env ready.'
// postAttachCommand: Runs EVERY time you attach a terminal/editor to the Codespace. Prints the welcome banner so the .env reminder is impossible to miss, even on a restart.
// SECRETS WARNING: Repository *Actions* secrets are NOT visible in a Codespaces terminal. Actions secrets and Codespaces secrets are two completely separate stores. Adding ICA_API_KEY under Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions only feeds the grader workflow; your Codespace terminal will still see nothing. To run code in here you must EITHER add a *Codespaces* secret named ICA_API_KEY (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Codespaces, then rebuild the container so it gets injected) OR paste your key into the .env file that postCreateCommand generated for you.
// secretsMetadata: Declaring the secret here makes GitHub prompt for it on the 'Create codespace' screen and show it under the Codespace's secret settings. It does NOT import Actions secrets.

ICA_API_KEY.description: Your IBM Consulting Advantage gateway key for api.servicesessentials.ibm.com. Set it as a Codespaces secret, or leave blank and paste it into .env instead.

vscode.// extensions: ms-python.python is the one that matters (interpreter, Run button, squiggles); the others make the course's .md lessons and .env file nicer to read.

// remoteUser: The base image's non-root user. pip installs land in its home, so no sudo needed.
